distractor_explanation.notes: FRQ; common errors are listed in the rubric rows.

exam_suitability.notes: Volume units of dollars^2/hour are meaningless; the item is not suitable as written.

review.summary: Rejected: the keyed crossing time 10.176 is wrong (the correct root is 9.537), so the keyed values for (b) and (d) are wrong too. The stimulus also has mismatched part labels and an unused revolution solid, and the volume has no meaningful units.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: The concepts are in scope (area between curves, square cross-section volume) and the item is a typical FRQ-style multi-part task. It requires solving f=g on a calculator, splitting the integral at the crossing and using the absolute difference, interpreting signed vs. total area, and setting up a squared-integrand volume. Representation changes are modest (table, function, integral, context), and the numbers are calculator-friendly. Flagged issues: the stimulus describes a revolved solid about y=-1 and 'intersection points' (plural), which conflicts with the squares in part d and with the single crossing; the units of area and volume (hours x dollars/hour) are awkward to interpret. These should be fixed before use, but they do not make the item hard.
